findings: IOC extraction omitted for email scans — the email route constructs ScanHistory directly and skips extract_iocs, so ioc_count is permanently 0 for all email rows in the history API. Add an ioc_list population step or pass an empty list explicitly to make the omission intentional and auditable.

Content-Length bypass allows full-buffer allocation — when a client omits the Content-Length header, request.content_length is None, the early gate is skipped, and the server allocates up to 5 MB + 1 bytes before rejecting. Consider setting app.config['MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH'] = 5 * 1024 * 1024 to enforce the cap at the WSGI layer.

No rate limiting on email upload — documented as intentional parity with other scan routes, but email analysis runs two ML models (message + per-link URL detector) per request, making it more expensive than APK or URL scans. Worth revisiting if the service is exposed publicly.
